title: Sleep & Strength
text:
CDC NHANES 2011–2014 · Ages 16 to 80+ · Observational Research Platform
    
    
      Rest & Resilience: Sleep Duration and Physical Strength Across the Human Lifespan
    
    
      An interactive empirical investigation of 10,987 U.S. adolescents, working-age adults, and older adults (ages 16–80+) examining how nightly sleep habits align with objective bilateral handgrip strength.
    

    
      Central Research Question
      
        How is sleep duration associated with physical strength, and does this relationship differ across age groups?
      
      
        Observational note: NHANES is a cross-sectional population survey. Associations documented here describe real-world population patterns and do not establish causal effects.
      
    
  

  
  
    
      Validated Sample
      10,987
      Complete sleep & bilateral grip exams across 2011–2014
    
    
      Age Coverage
      16–80+ yrs
      Youth (16+), prime working-age, and older adulthood
    
    
      Mean Nightly Sleep
      6.91 hrs
      54.3% report the recommended 7–8 hours/night
    
    
      Combined Grip Strength
      70.8 kg
      Mean sum of max left + right hand dynamometry (median 67.0 kg)

          Smoothed topographic strength surface across seven life-stage bands (ages 16–80+) and seven sleep-duration tiers. Hover any cell for exact sample counts, means, and interquartile ranges, or switch to inspect all 10,987 individual participants.

    Data Provenance & Measurement
    CDC NHANES 2011–2014 Dataset & Variables
    
      Data combine two consecutive waves of the U.S. National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (2011–2012 Cycle G and 2013–2014 Cycle H), merging demographics, self-reported sleep questionnaires (administered to participants aged 16 and older), and Mobile Examination Center (MEC) isometric grip dynamometry.
    

    
      
        SLD010H · Sleep Questionnaire
        Nightly Sleep Duration
        
          Self-reported usual weekday/workday sleep hours (integer values 2 through 12+, with NHANES codes 77 Refused and 99 Don't Know recoded as missing). Categorized into Very Short (≤5h), Short (6h), Recommended (7–8h), and Long (9+h).
        
      
      
        MGDCGSZ · Takei Dynamometer
        Combined Grip Strength (kg)
        
          Objective upper-body isometric muscle strength measured across three trials per hand. Defined by CDC protocol as the sum of the largest reading from each hand (ranging from 8.0 kg to 169.6 kg in our validated sample).
        
      
      
        RIDAGEYR & RIAGENDR · Demographics
        Age Across the Lifespan (16–80+)
        
          Covers late adolescence through older adulthood: ages 16–29 (n = 2,959), 30–44 (n = 2,592), 45–59 (n = 2,422), 60–74 (n = 2,118), and 75–80+ (n = 896; CDC top-codes ages 80 and over at 80).
